title: Mom takes the bike
setting: A Saturday. Yuki's mother is coming up from the countryside to visit Yuki's flat. Yuki phones her while she's on the train, and later her mother calls back from the station.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.ja: もしもし、お母さん？もう電車乗った？
lines.kana: もしもし、おかあさん？もうでんしゃのった？
lines.english: Hello, Mom? Are you on the train yet?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: notta yo. densha ni noru no, honto ni hisashiburi.
lines.ja: 乗ったよ。電車に乗るの、ほんとに久しぶり。
lines.kana: のったよ。でんしゃにのるの、ほんとにひさしぶり。
lines.english: Yep, I'm on. It's been ages since I last rode a train.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: da yo ne. okaasan, mainichi jitensha ni notteru mon ne.
lines.ja: だよね。お母さん、毎日自転車に乗ってるもんね。
lines.kana: だよね。おかあさん、まいにちじてんしゃにのってるもんね。
lines.english: I bet. You're on your bike every day, after all.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: un. de, doko de densha oriru n da kke?
lines.ja: うん。で、どこで電車降りるんだっけ？
lines.kana: うん。で、どこででんしゃおりるんだっけ？
lines.english: Mm. So where do I get off the train again?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: mittsume da yo. eki made kuruma de ikou ka?
lines.ja: 三つ目だよ。駅まで車で行こうか？
lines.kana: みっつめだよ。えきまでくるまでいこうか？
lines.english: The third stop. Want me to drive to the station?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: ii yo, ii yo. basu ni noru kara daijoubu.
lines.ja: いいよ、いいよ。バスに乗るから大丈夫。
lines.kana: いいよ、いいよ。ばすにのるからだいじょうぶ。
lines.english: No, no, it's fine. I'll take the bus.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jaa, densha o oritara, eki de basu ni notte ne.
lines.ja: じゃあ、電車を降りたら、駅でバスに乗ってね。
lines.kana: じゃあ、でんしゃをおりたら、えきでばすにのってね。
lines.english: Okay. Then once you're off the train, get on the bus at the station.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: moshimoshi, yuki? densha wa orita n da kedo.
lines.ja: もしもし、ユキ？電車は降りたんだけど。
lines.kana: もしもし、ゆき？でんしゃはおりたんだけど。
lines.english: Hello, Yuki? Well, I got off the train, but...

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.ja: え、まだバス乗ってないの？
lines.kana: え、まだばすのってないの？
lines.english: What, you're still not on the bus?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: sore ga ne, basu ga zutto konai no yo.
lines.ja: それがね、バスがずっと来ないのよ。
lines.kana: それがね、ばすがずっとこないのよ。
lines.english: Well, that's the thing. The bus just isn't coming.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: honto ni? jaa, ima kara kuruma notte iku kara, eki ni ite ne.
lines.ja: ほんとに？じゃあ、今から車乗っていくから、駅にいてね。
lines.kana: ほんとに？じゃあ、いまからくるまのっていくから、えきにいてね。
lines.english: Seriously? Then I'll get in the car and come right now. Stay at the station.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: ii no, ii no. eki ni, rentaru no jitensha ga aru no yo.
lines.ja: いいの、いいの。駅に、レンタルの自転車があるのよ。
lines.kana: いいの、いいの。えきに、れんたるのじてんしゃがあるのよ。
lines.english: No need, no need. There are rental bikes at the station.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, okaasan, jitensha ni notte kuru no?
lines.ja: え、お母さん、自転車に乗ってくるの？
lines.kana: え、おかあさん、じてんしゃにのってくるの？
lines.english: What? Mom, you're going to ride a bike all the way here?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: un. jitensha de iku kara, daijoubu.
lines.ja: うん。自転車で行くから、大丈夫。
lines.kana: うん。じてんしゃでいくから、だいじょうぶ。
lines.english: Yep. I'll go by bike, so don't worry.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: demo watashi, mou kuruma ni notchatta yo.
lines.ja: でも私、もう車に乗っちゃったよ。
lines.kana: でもわたし、もうくるまにのっちゃったよ。
lines.english: But I've already got in the car!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: jaa, sono kuruma de kaimono ni itte kite. okaasan, onaka suichatta.
lines.ja: じゃあ、その車で買い物に行ってきて。お母さん、お腹すいちゃった。
lines.kana: じゃあ、そのくるまでかいものにいってきて。おかあさん、おなかすいちゃった。
lines.english: Then take the car and go do the shopping. Mom's starving.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hai hai. demo kaeri wa, watashi no kuruma ni notte ne!
lines.ja: はいはい。でも帰りは、私の車に乗ってね！
lines.kana: はいはい。でもかえりは、わたしのくるまにのってね！
lines.english: Fine, fine. But on the way back, you're riding in my car!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: hai hai. jaa, jitensha ni notte iku ne!
lines.ja: はいはい。じゃあ、自転車に乗っていくね！
lines.kana: はいはい。じゃあ、じてんしゃにのっていくね！
lines.english: Fine, fine. Right, I'm off on the bike!

questions.english: What happens in these two phone calls?

choices.english: Mom gets off the train at the wrong stop, so Yuki drives out to fetch her.
The bus doesn't come, so Mom decides to ride a rental bike over, and Yuki, already in her car, goes shopping instead.
The bus doesn't come, so Yuki drives to the station, picks Mom up and takes her shopping.

questions.explanation: Lines 8-10: Mom has got off the train (densha wa orita n da kedo), but the bus just isn't coming (basu ga zutto konai no yo). Line 11: Yuki offers to come in the car, but in line 12 Mom says there are rental bikes at the station, and in lines 13-14 she says she'll go by bike (jitensha de iku). Line 15: Yuki is already in the car (mou kuruma ni notchatta yo), so in line 16 Mom sends her shopping. A is wrong: nothing goes wrong with the stop; the problem is the bus (line 10), and Yuki never fetches her. C is wrong: Mom turns down the car twice (lines 6 and 12), Yuki goes shopping on her own (line 16), and Mom will only ride in Yuki's car on the way back (line 17).

questions.english: Yuki phones while you're on your way to meet her: "moshimoshi, ima doko ni iru no?" (Hello, where are you right now?) You're on the train. Tell her.
questions.ja: もしもし、今どこにいるの？
questions.kana: もしもし、いまどこにいるの？
questions.romaji: moshimoshi, ima doko ni iru no?
questions.answer: Say you're on the train right now with densha ni noru in its -teru form: ima, densha notteru yo.

modelAnswers.english: I'm on the train right now.
I'm on the train right now.

questions.explanation: Being on a train is densha ni noru, and the -teru form (notteru, nottemasu) says you're riding it right now. The vehicle takes ni, never o, and 'take the train' is never toru. Line 1 uses the past: mou densha notta? (have you got on the train yet?), and in line 2 Mom answers notta yo. For 'where are you?', notteru fits better: it's where you are now. Casual speech often drops ni, as Yuki does in line 1. The second model is the polite version, for someone like Tanaka-san.

questions.english: Yuki offers to drive to the station, and her mother turns her down. What did her mother say?
questions.ja: お母さんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: おかあさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: No, no, it's fine. I'll take the bus.
choices.romaji: ii yo, ii yo. basu ni noru kara daijoubu.

choices.english: No, no, it's fine. I'll take the bus. (toru: take as in pick up, grab)
choices.romaji: ii yo, ii yo. basu o toru kara daijoubu.

choices.english: No, no, it's fine. I'll ride the bus. (the bus as an object, with o)
choices.romaji: ii yo, ii yo. basu o noru kara daijoubu.

questions.explanation: Line 6: Mom says basu ni noru kara daijoubu. Every vehicle takes ni noru, so the bus is marked with ni. B is English 'take the bus' put word for word into Japanese: toru is take as in pick up or grab, and you never toru a bus. C keeps noru but marks the bus with o, the way English 'ride the bus' takes an object; noru always marks the vehicle with ni. Yuki uses the same frame in line 7 (basu ni notte ne) and line 9 (mada basu nottenai no?).

questions.english: You and Kenta are heading out in your car. You went out first and you're already sitting in it. Kenta calls from the door: "mou deru yo! doko?" (I'm leaving now! Where are you?) Tell him you're already in the car.
questions.answer: Say you're already in the car with kuruma ni noru in its -teru form: mou kuruma notteru yo!

modelAnswers.ja: もう車に乗ってますよ。

questions.explanation: Getting into a car and sitting in it are both kuruma ni noru; notteru says you're in it now. Not kuruma ni hairu: hairu is for going into a room or a building, and kuruma no naka ni hairu is only ducking inside, say out of the rain. Yuki says it with -chatta in line 15 (mou kuruma ni notchatta yo, I've already got in the car), and in line 17 she uses it for riding along: kaeri wa, watashi no kuruma ni notte ne. The second model is the polite version, for someone like Tanaka-san.

questions.english: Mai is meeting you at the station. You've just stepped off the train when she calls: "moshimoshi, ima doko? mada densha?" (Hello, where are you? Still on the train?) Tell her no, you've got off the train.
questions.ja: もしもし、今どこ？まだ電車？
questions.kana: もしもし、いまどこ？まだでんしゃ？
questions.answer: Say no, you're already off, with oriru in the past and the train marked by o (or the o dropped): uun, mou densha orita yo.

modelAnswers.ja: ううん、もう電車降りたよ。
modelAnswers.english: Nope, I've already got off the train.

modelAnswers.ja: いいえ、もう電車を降りました。
modelAnswers.english: No, I've already got off the train.

questions.explanation: Getting off is oriru, and the train takes o: densha o oriru, the other half of the pair with densha ni noru. Yuki says both in one breath in line 7: densha o oritara, eki de basu ni notte ne (once you're off the train, get on the bus at the station). Not densha ni oriru, and not densha kara deru. Casual speech often drops the o, as Mom does in line 4 (doko de densha oriru n da kke?), and in line 8 she uses wa instead: densha wa orita n da kedo (I did get off the train, but...). The second model is the polite version, for someone like Tanaka-san.

questions.english: Mom says there are rental bikes at the station, and Yuki asks, "e, okaasan, jitensha ni notte kuru no?" What is Mom going to do?
questions.ja: お母さんは何をしますか？
questions.kana: おかあさんはなにをしますか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa nani o shimasu ka?

choices.english: She has already cycled over and is nearly at Yuki's place.
She wants Yuki to come to the station by bike instead of by car.
She is going to ride a bike from the station all the way to Yuki's place.

questions.explanation: Line 13: jitensha ni notte kuru is 'come here riding a bike', and Yuki can hardly believe her mother means to cycle over from the station. In line 14 Mom confirms it, with de for how she'll travel (jitensha de iku), and in line 18 she sets off (jitensha ni notte iku ne!). A would be notte kita, 'has come by bike'; Mom is still at the station with the rental bikes (line 12). B is wrong: Yuki is the one with the car (lines 11 and 15), and nobody asks her to cycle. Line 3 explains why Mom is so keen: she rides her bike every day (mainichi jitensha ni notteru).

newWords.english: the third (one); here, the third stop (mittsu = three, -me = -th)
as far as, to (eki made = to the station)
rental (rentaru no jitensha = a rental bike)
say (nan to iimashita ka? = what did she say?)
